source: A21 Secret capacity stage after c6748fd; pre-commit working tree

correctedBoundary.old: Full lists had per-namespace 32-MiB/10,000-item/15-second limits and flat summaries retained all namespace values through Promise.all. Twenty large supported objects could exceed the four-MiB response cap.
correctedBoundary.new: One-object pages are visited immediately for metadata projection. All selected namespaces read sequentially with one shared 32-MiB accepted-wire/10,000-item/15-second budget, and remaining bytes constrain response buffering before JSON parsing.
correctedBoundary.unchanged: Four-MiB individual response cap, four-active/64-queued global native request pool, eight-second individual deadline, TLS verification, exact key names, immutable/type/identity metadata and fresh/CAS value gates

proofs: Complete 100-namespace compatibility fixture shares the same budget/deadline object, uses one active list at most, and returns no values/annotations
Cross-namespace item and byte overflows fail with fixed 503 and do not start later namespaces; invalid/expired budgets fail closed
Verified TLS fixture visits 124 objects across 100 namespaces without returning retained full objects; one active list request at most, no value-bearing summary or leftover pool work
Verified TLS aggregate byte overflow across individually valid namespaces stops before the fourth namespace; response buffering observes remaining aggregate bytes
Twenty synthetic 256-KiB history objects exceed four MiB as a full list, while 25-object metadata-only enumeration succeeds

Protocol fixture creates 25 real owned maximum-size versions through normal versioned mutations; GC preview finds 24 old unreferenced candidates while full history listing is forbidden. Stale-RV cleanup refuses without deletion; refreshed cleanup uses exact UID/RV and preserves canonical/head data

Existing 40-object pagination still returns all objects through 40 one-object pages; repeated cursors, oversize replies, values in metadata negotiation and missing/wrong history preconditions remain rejected
A short shared native deadline releases active/queued work without completing the collection

requestCost.fixture: 334 small synthetic objects across 18 namespaces; verified loopback TLS and fixed 12-ms producer delay
requestCost.interpretation: The old page count is arithmetic only, not a timed baseline. One-object paging materially increases request cost; this is a capacity correction, not an unqualified performance improvement. Slower APIs can hit the unchanged 15-second aggregate deadline.

tableOption.reviewed: Official Table negotiation and exact Kubernetes v1.37.1 Secret printer
tableOption.decision: Retain the current exact-key-name/immutable/CAS metadata contract in this stage. Table cells contain key count rather than names, so adoption requires explicit selected-object metadata retrieval and caller migration. No Table/object-inclusion/fallback path is implemented.

corrections: Initial capacity fixture type checking rejected incomplete transport casts; fixtures now provide explicit refusing value/mutation methods without changing assertions
limitations: No live cluster, production limits, credentials, DB, deployment or inventory cleanup was changed
334 objects is a synthetic fixture based on reported baseline size, not a refreshed production count
Wire budgets and deterministic retained-object/concurrency proofs are not a 32-MiB process RSS promise
Host CPU/RSS and network were not isolated; controlled Linux memory/live latency acceptance remains open
Individual supported objects do not imply every arbitrarily large collection fits the unchanged byte/item/deadline limits; over-limit collections fail explicitly
A21 Secret/child table DOM bounds, full KV UI, final Linux/recovery artifact and live admission/RBAC remain pending
